headline: Highest risk is medium: shared filesystem and API-driven research workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and output-cascade paths, but no evidence of default irreversible harm.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and gpt-researcher reads files, PDFs, and MCP/API inputs. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled content from B can be ingested by A as instructions, especially if outputs are exchanged through shared files or MCP. No stronger isolation is documented for either agent.
conditions: IF the pair exchanges files, Markdown, or MCP messages without provenance tags
IF gpt-researcher ingests untrusted web or document content into a shared workspace
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable MCP sharing between the agents
Prefix all inter-agent files with a non-executable header
Manually review any file before AutoGPT consumes it
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking to shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files, and gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents plus multiple third-party APIs. If AutoGPT places sensitive files in a shared workspace, B can read them and transmit contents to external services. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary or local-only inference, so leakage is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or mounted volume
IF sensitive documents are present in files that gpt-researcher can read
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Run gpt-researcher with network egress blocked for sensitive tasks
Use separate OS users for each agent
Rotate or scope API keys to non-sensitive projects
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses; gpt-researcher can install packages, run browsers, and also spawn subprocesses. In a shared directory or orchestrated session, overlapping write-capable actions can race on files, dependencies, or generated artifacts. No locking or coordination primitive is documented for the pair.
conditions: IF both agents write into the same project directory
IF package installation or shell commands run concurrently without locks
mitigations: Serialize write operations
Use separate virtual environments
Assign each agent a distinct working directory
Avoid concurrent package installs
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared outputs

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher has planner/execution/publisher roles and can turn upstream outputs into reports or actions; AutoGPT can generate intermediate artifacts that B may treat as authoritative. Because no verification step or provenance control is documented, a bad A output can cascade into B-produced research deliverables or downstream actions. The interaction is therefore dangerous by default.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher consumes AutoGPT-generated text as source material
IF the publisher step forwards unverified claims into reports or actions
mitigations: Require human review before publishing
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted input
Add a verification checklist before B publishes
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add citation/provenance validation

E_compliance.rationale: gpt-researcher explicitly handles local documents, citations, and multiple external APIs, while AutoGPT can access the filesystem and network. If regulated documents are placed in the shared workflow, B may transmit them to third-party services, creating a compliance mismatch. AutoGPT is open-source and not itself a residency control, so the risk centers on B's external processing.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound documents are processed by gpt-researcher
IF those documents are sent to OpenAI, Tavily, Gemini, or LangChain-backed services
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from research tasks
Use a local-only deployment for B
Disable external API calls for sensitive runs
Document retention and deletion settings
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing
